text: Ordered during a heavy drizzle, took 95 minutes to reach and the cappuccino was cold as the rain outside. Done with wet-evening orders.
Fries reached me as a sad wet lump - the box had collapsed in the rain and everything inside was stone cold.
Fifteen minutes for a single espresso while it poured outside, and the counter staff just chatted. Missed my cab.
Walked in soaked hoping for a cosy corner. Wet slippery floor, no free table, and nobody even looked up for ten minutes.
Kulhad chai bilkul paani jaisi thi aaj, no ginger kick at all. 140 rupaye barbaad in this weather.
Half our order never arrived - the strawberry shake and one pasta missing, kids waited hungry till 9. Rain is no excuse for a wrong bag.
Filter coffee tasted burnt today, like old decoction reheated. Gloomy Monday or not, this is not the brew I know.
Twelve-item office order in the rain: three drinks missing, lids loose, chai leaked through the kraft bag onto the sandwiches.
Monsoon evening and every table had wet umbrellas dumped on chairs. Our flat whites took 25 minutes to reach a sticky table.
Rain pushed the whole crowd indoors; stood 20 minutes with my laptop, no seat, nobody offered a waitlist. Left drenched and annoyed.
Rider took forever and the waffle arrived a soggy cold sponge, maple syrup leaked through the bag. Tragic end to a rainy day.
Needed a quick cappuccino before a meeting in this downpour - 18 minutes at the counter. Completely pointless.
Chai aur fries 300 ke, aur woh bhi thande. Baarish mein comfort chahiye tha, pocket mein hole nahi.
Hot chocolate reached half-spilled inside the bag, cup lid had popped, everything sticky. Rainy evening properly ruined.
Kids soaked and hungry, waited 30 minutes for one cheese toast while Zoya chatted at the till. Nobody even apologised.
Usually love this place, but today's cappuccino was watery and there were rain puddles under my table. Hoping it was an off day.
Pink walls cannot fix a stale muffin and a dripping window seat. Wanted a rainy-day treat, got damp socks instead.
Baarish bahar, queue andar. Ek flat white 12 minute mein aaya kyunki staff ticket printer pe argue kar rahe the. V slow.
Delivery took 70 minutes in the drizzle; paneer tikka sandwich was cold and the mint chutney had turned weird.
Iced latte turned up half empty - lid was not sealed and the kraft bag was soaked through. What survived tasted fine.
Two tired kids, wet jackets, and a twenty-five minute wait for shakes. The strawberry shake itself was lovely when it finally came.
Har table pe log ek chai leke do ghante baithe hain. Exam time aur baarish - seat milna impossible hai.
Team order of nine drinks: two cappuccinos came as espressos and nothing was labelled. Wet bags made the mix-up worse.
Cheese toast arrived cold and rubbery, probably the rain delay. The peri-peri fries underneath were still decent though.
Heard it was a hidden gem, but 270 for a rose latte that tasted mostly of plain milk? Cute spot, steep bill, wet shoes.
Croissant was clearly from yesterday - chewy, not flaky. Service was quick at least, and Kabir is always polite.
Laptop day ruined by the rain crowd: one working plug and the blender screeching every minute. Cold brew was the only good part.
Stormy-night dinner took 80 minutes and the pasta was barely lukewarm. The arrabbiata sauce itself had real kick, to be fair.
Team ka bulk pickup evening rush mein bahut late hua, aur do cinnamon rolls bag se gayab the.
Matcha was clumpy and barely warm on a wet afternoon. The window seat watching the rain made it almost bearable.
Everything arrived sideways - strawberry shake leaked into the waffle box. Cold, soggy, sad.
Flat white was genuinely excellent and the pink nook is adorable in the rain, but we waited twenty minutes for it.
Rain delayed the rider 40 minutes; chai was warmish not hot, but the cinnamon roll survived and tasted fresh.
Chai aur cheese toast mast the, par baarish mein sab andar aa gaye - seat bilkul nahi mili. Thoda cramped.
Slow counter this rainy morning - ten minutes for a cappuccino - but the microfoam was perfect as always.
Hot chocolate tipped slightly in the bag but the pasta was still warm and the kids fought over the marshmallows.
Wet-afternoon crowd means zero free plugs and loud chatter everywhere; the cold brew and the corner I finally grabbed were worth it.
Fifteen-item monsoon order: one sandwich came wrong, the rest were spot on and still warm. Labels on the bags genuinely helped.
Filter coffee abhi bhi best hai 120 mein, but croissant ke daam phir se chupke se badh gaye. Hmm.
Took an hour in the rain; the avocado toast arrived intact and tasted fresh, just not remotely warm.
Ducked in from the rain to pure cosy - pink walls, steam on the windows. Queue was long and my filter coffee came lukewarm.
Baarish ke din line kaafi lambi thi. Fries garam the aur cheap bhi - bas time laga. Theek hai overall.
Meera was so sweet when my daughter spilled her shake, but the food took 30 minutes on a wet Tuesday.
Baarish mein order thanda ho gaya tha, lekin packing solid thi - kuch bhi spill nahi hua. Fries bas crispy nahi the.
Wet-morning rush means slow tickets out the kitchen; the espresso itself was punchy and well pulled.
Office tea run: all eight drinks labelled and dry despite the rain, but one matcha arrived as a regular latte.
Rainy window vibes toh great hain, but 290 for a matcha is steep yaar. Student budget crying a little.
Grabbed a croissant between showers; a bit dense today, though Kabir remembered my usual which was a sweet touch.
Kids' dinner run took 65 minutes in the downpour, but the fries were still crisp and the shake nice and thick.
Rainy laptop afternoon: lovely window light and decent wifi, but my ticket got lost once and the music was loud.
Cappuccino 220 ka - is rate pe morning coffee cab ride se mehengi ho jayegi. Speed theek thi at least.
Rose milk was refreshing even in this weather; the waffle next to it arrived chewy and cold though.
Filter coffee in the rain - peak Bengaluru. Just a shame I stood fifteen minutes waiting for it.
Iced latte solid tha, but delivery charges milake 300 plus ho gaya. Pocket friendly nahi hai yeh.
Rainy crowd was loud and our little table wobbled; the strawberry cheesecake, though, was close to perfect.
Rainy Saturday, corner table, a flat white with a perfect heart. Small wait but who cares with that view.
In and out in four minutes despite the wet-morning crowd, espresso hot and strong. Knocking one off for the leaky cup sleeve.
Impressed - heavy rain and it still arrived in 45 minutes, chai steaming and the muffin dry in its box.
Baarish, kulhad chai aur cheese toast - perfect combo under 350. Sirf seats thodi kam hain.
Camped three hours through a downpour; refilled cold brew, got a plug near the window, and nobody rushed me once.
Evening rain delayed it 15 minutes but the pasta was properly hot and the kids demolished the fries.
Kabir saw me walk in dripping and had a filter coffee going before I sat down. Bill took a while, small thing.
Ten labelled kraft bags, all bone dry despite the rain, every single drink correct. Pickup queue could move faster.
Expected a soggy mess in this weather; the sandwich was warm and the chutney punchy. Fries softened a little.
Monsoon in Bengaluru, a dabarah of filter coffee, pink walls - this little place just gets it.
Wet, cranky kids were pacified with quick shakes and a window table. The two-seaters are a bit small for four of us.
Cheese toast aur chai combo abhi bhi affordable hai, aur itni baarish mein bhi garam aaya. Solid yaar.
Waffle with maple while it poured outside - crisp edges, warm centre. Service was gentle, just slightly slow.
Rainy-day order for twelve: every cup labelled, one item ran late but they called ahead. Reliable bunch.
Usual cappuccino ready in three minutes, heart intact, and a warm towel for my wet hands. Almost perfect.
Ducked in soaked with my laptop; espresso pulled fast and properly. Only gripe - nowhere to park a wet umbrella.
Hot chocolate sealed tight, zero spills, marshmallows intact after a rainy ride across town. Genuinely impressive packing.
Rain pe chill karne ke liye best spot hai yeh. Filter coffee sasta aur strong. WiFi bas thoda slow tha.
Cold brew travelled surprisingly well - sealed cup, orange twist still fresh. The fries softened a bit in the steam.
Rainy Tuesday, got the good corner, warm staff, stable wifi for two calls. Music crept a bit loud at midday.
Chai ekdum mast thi auto se pehle - spicy, milky, is mausam ke liye perfect. Double cup sleeve nice touch.
Wet window, warm matcha, a slice of Basque cheesecake. Nearly perfect rainy afternoon; the seats just fill fast.
Kids' dinner arrived quicker than quoted despite the rain, pasta still steaming. Portions run modest though.
Consistency is why I keep returning - the same silky flat white every visit, even when the floor is full of wet footprints.
Iced latte 35 minute mein aaya, ice bhi melt nahi hui somehow. Paisa vasool for a rainy study night.
Rapid counter service this morning; the lidded cup survived a full dash through the rain without losing a drop.
Rain outside, warmth inside - kids split a waffle, we shared two filter coffees. Cosy, just slightly cramped.
Eight drinks for a wet afternoon meeting - all correct, still warm, just ten minutes past the estimate.
Rose milk with sabja on a rainy day should not work but somehow it does. Charming little pink box of a cafe.
Third wet-weather order this month and the bags arrive dry, drinks hot, labels clear every time. Consistent crew.
Do chais lectures ke beech - under 300 total aur minutes mein nikal gaye. Queue moves even when it pours.
Monsoon playlist, steamed windows, a shared cinnamon roll. Only gripe - they had run out of muffins by 4pm.
Rain hammering the windows, a flat white with a perfect heart, and absolutely nowhere to be. brew is my happy place.
Downpour outside and my order still reached hot in 40 minutes - sealed cup, dry bag, fresh cinnamon roll. Flawless.
Soaked and running late, still got my espresso in ninety seconds flat. This team does not miss.
Meera spotted me at the door and started my cappuccino before I said a word. Fifth rainy Tuesday in a row.
Delivery in heavy rain and the fries were STILL crispy. Hot chocolate sealed like a lab sample. Kids thrilled.
Baarish, kulhad chai aur window seat - perfect evening boss. 140 mein itna sukoon kahan milta hai.
Sixteen drinks, one soggy walk back to office, zero errors, every label legible. Flawless bulk run.
Caught in a storm, found brew. Filter coffee frothed in a dabarah while rain lashed outside - pure Bengaluru magic.
Monsoon workday done right: plug, window, cold brew refills, and zero pressure to leave. Three productive hours.
Rider braved a proper downpour - sandwich warm, chutney packed separately, bag stamped and dry. Ten out of ten.
Staff mopped up my son's spilled shake with a smile and brought a fresh one on the house. Kindness tastes sweet.
Evening drizzle, queue of six, out in five minutes with a cappuccino that made the wet commute worth it.
Watching monsoon rain through brew's steamy window with a rose latte in hand - this is the Indiranagar dream.
Itni baarish mein bhi cheese toast garam aaya. 260 mein khushi delivered. Love this place.
Quoted 60, arrived in 38, iced latte perfectly chilled and not watery at all. Rain or shine, they deliver.
Ten years of Bengaluru cafes and nothing beats a rainy morning here - the same perfect filter coffee, same warm faces.
Wet shoes, happy kids, a shared waffle and a thick strawberry shake. The pink warmth hits different on a grey day.
Storm-day team order of fourteen, arrived early, every cup labelled with names. Zero chaos, all caffeine.
Ducked in to escape the rain and three minutes later had a flawless flat white and a dry stool by the door.
Ordered to the hotel on a rainy night - cheesecake arrived pristine, not a smudge on the strawberry glaze. Beautiful.
Chai, fries, thunder bahar, best seat in the house. 300 rupaye well spent. Kal phir aaunga.
Zoya had my ticket printing before I finished shaking out my umbrella. Home is not a place, it is a counter.
Waffle survived a long ride in the rain - still crisp-edged, maple in a separate pot. A detail-obsessed kitchen.
Cinnamon roll warm, icing melting, rain streaking the glass. I could honestly write poetry here.
Rainy-night order: pasta hot, shake thick, delivered in thirty minutes. The kids call it the pink food.
Camped through the entire afternoon storm; refills appeared unprompted and nobody hovered. Rare respect for laptop folks.
Masala chai mast thi pouring rain mein - spicy, sweet, soul-warming. Bengaluru, well played.
Do baar order kiya is wet week mein, dono baar garam aur intact aaya. Kraft bags umbrellas se zyada sturdy hain.
Every visit, rain or shine, the flat white tastes identical - silky, strong, poured with care. That is the whole review.
Garam chai aur crispy fries baarish mein, 35 min flat mein delivered. Best study-night combo, sach mein.
Stormy evening, warm lights, and patient staff who did not blink at our loud kids. The strawberry shake was divine.
First Bengaluru monsoon, ordered in from the guesthouse - cold brew with the orange twist still bright. I get the hype.
If heaven is a place, it is this window seat in the rain with a hot chocolate and nowhere to go.
